criteria.notes: The landscape kiosk provides searchable destinations, full authored 3D overview, complete exploded route, camera journey, live status, replay, accessibility profile, language, and visitor-triggered audio without Atlas or step controls.

Map pixels, polygon colors, backgrounds, labels, media, floor explosion, route hierarchy, and camera rendering come from the canonical Editor Preview primitives rather than a custom map approximation.
The result reads as a dedicated architectural directory: persistent destination rail, map-dominant center stage, and restrained destination context instead of a generic dashboard.
All declared near-touch primary, secondary, and metadata selectors pass their computed font floors; route and destination actions remain legible at 1920x1080.
Dark, light, and custom shell palettes retain clear hierarchy and controls while leaving the authored map presentation unchanged.
The long welcome prompt wraps to four readable lines, the long venue identity ellipsizes cleanly, and destination/status policies pass without clipping.
The fixed Full HD composition consistently measures 98% width and 100% height content coverage; the directory scroll region is intentional and touch reachable.
Published map imagery and destination photography render sharply, route contrast survives the exploded building view, and both shell themes appear installation-ready.
No legacy wayfinding example was used as a visual template; the shell is purpose-built around the new canonical viewer boundary and supplied map.
